facts: BLOMER-PASCADI Theorem 1.1 (arXiv:2607.24311v1, verbatim): Let c in Z_{>0}, N in Z cap [1,c], I, J in Z intervals with |I|,|J| <= N. Then for any complex sequences (alpha_m), (beta_n) and any a in (Z/cZ)^x:  sum_{(m,n) in I x J, (m,n,c)=1} alpha_m beta_n S(am,n;c)  <<  ||alpha|| ||beta|| c^{1+o(1)} ( N^{1/8}/c^{3/32} + N^{5/16}/c^{3/16} + N^{2/3}/c^{7/18} )  =  ||alpha|| ||beta|| N c^{1/2+o(1)} ( c^{13/32}/N^{7/8} + c^{5/16}/N^{11/16} + c^{1/9}/N^{1/3} ), where S(am,n;c) is the Kloosterman sum. If I = J = {1,...,N} the bound holds WITHOUT the (m,n,c)=1 constraint. Trivial bounds in the same paper: (1.1) Weil: ||alpha|| ||beta|| N c^{1/2+o(1)}; (1.2) open-and-Cauchy: ||alpha|| ||beta|| (c+N). At N = c^{1/2} (critical): all three BP terms are c^{-1/32}, c^{-1/32}, c^{-1/18} times N c^{1/2} (min saving c^{-1/32+o(1)}) - BEATING BOTH trivial bounds (at N = c^{1/2} the trivial bounds coincide at N c^{1/2} = c^{3/4}). Valid for ALL moduli c (squarefree part by the new quadratic-character method, Theorem 5.2; squarefull part by [Pascadi, Theorem 7.1]; combined factorization-freely in Theorem 5.5).

PRZZ section 4 bookkeeping (arXiv:1802.10521, extracted to full depth): the Type II sum is sum_{0<|a|<A} nu(a) sum_{v ~ V, (v,h)=1} r(v) sum_{e ~ E, f ~ F, (ef,v)=1} alpha(e) beta(f) e(-a * hbar u / v) with EF ~ U, W << E << F << U W^{-1}; the dyadic decomposition gives U ~ N1/dh and V ~ N2/d (N1, N2 the [58] factorization of the main length N); n1 splits n1 = h n1' with h | d^infinity, h << N1/d, G(h) weight |G(h)| << tau(dh)^{O(1)} (log N)^{O(1)}, and sum_{h|d^infinity} G(h)/h^eps << (dT)^eps; the Type I estimate (summation by parts + Weil bound for incomplete Kloosterman sums) is (1+|w|) T^eps (A V^{3/2} W + A U V^{1/2}) with W << (N1/dh)^{1/3} free; the Type II estimate is Deshouillers-Iwaniec Lemma 1 (Acta Arith. 48 (1984)) SEVEN-TERM: E^{-1/2}A^{1/2}U V + h^{1/4}A U V^{1/2} + h^{1/4}E^{1/4}A^{3/4}U V^{1/2} + h^{1/4}E^{-1/4}A U^{3/4}V + h^{1/2}E^{1/4}A U^{3/4}V^{3/4} + h^{1/4}E^{1/4}A^{1/2}U^{3/4}V + h^{1/2}E^{3/4}A^{1/2}U^{3/4}V^{3/4}; the proof SETS W = U^{1/4} to balance Type I and Type II, uses E^{-a} << U^{-a/4} (a<0) and E^{b} << U^{b/2} (b>0), and requires (hidden-h constraint) that in each term the power of h is smaller than the power of U (U ~ N1/dh carries a hidden h; a net positive power of h must remain in the denominator to sum over h); the final bound is A*_{M,N1,N2} << T^eps/d (T^{1/2} N^{7/8} + N^{7/4}) and the admissible choice is N = T^{4/7-eps}. A (the a-sum length) is carried from [58]; the paper says 'We assume familiarity with [58] and its notation'.

APPLICABILITY SHAPE (confirmed by inspection): BP Theorem 1.1 plugs exactly at the Kloosterman-bilinear step of each v-level of the Type II sum (its (m,n) = the paper's (e,f)-pair up to the (ef,v)=1 re-indexing; modulus c = v). Its all-moduli, factorization-free, no-coprimality-needed (full interval case) form is EXACTLY what the v-sum over v ~ V with (v,h)=1 needs. Since at the critical bilateral length N_bp ~ v^{1/2} (which holds per-v for the dominant h ~ 1 contribution when U ~ V, i.e. N1/(N2 h) ~ 1) BP beats BOTH classical trivial bounds (Weil N v^{1/2} and open-and-Cauchy v + N_bp) simultaneously, any DI term whose Kloosterman step runs in that regime is improvable by the BP factor; the terms E^{-1/2}A^{1/2}UV (the h-free term, pure Weil side) and the h^{1/2} E^{3/4} A^{1/2} U^{3/4} V^{3/4} type terms (the c+N side) are the two structural anchors.

THE BLOCKING UNKNOWN (precisely located, for the deep-read): the PRZZ section 4 proof is COMPRESSED and does not enumerate which of the seven DI terms (and which Type I terms) reduce, after W = U^{1/4} and U ~ N1/dh, V ~ N2/d substitution, to the final T^{1/2} N^{7/8} term and which to the N^{7/4} term. That term-by-term power arithmetic is delegated to [58] (the Pratt-Robles companion that fixes the A, N1, N2, M sizes). The N^{7/4} side is the bilinear-Kloosterman side per the 0304 audit; the exact exponent transfer from a per-v saving (c^{-1/32+o(1)} at U ~ V) to a final N-saving (delta or delta2 in the LevWall7 double-waste formula 4/7 + min(8 delta/7, 4 delta2/7)) requires that bookkeeping.
